qs.q: The ICAO Annex that deals with the entry and departure of persons, their baggage, cargo and other articles on international flights is:
o: Annex 9
Annex 15
Annex 8

qs.q: For aircraft of other Contracting States not on scheduled services, flying across a State or stopping for non-traffic purposes, the State accepts the flight plan as adequate advance notification. It must be received:
o: At least 2 hours before arrival
At least 4 hours before arrival
At least 1 hour before arrival

qs.q: A State that still requires a cargo manifest shall not require, beyond the heading information, more than:
o: The air waybill number and the number of packages for it
The air waybill number, the number of packages for each air waybill and the nature of the goods
The air waybill number and the nature of the goods

qs.q: A non-scheduled aircraft admitted temporarily free of duty to a designated airport of a Contracting State shall be allowed to remain without security for customs duty:
o: For 12 hours
For 48 hours
For a period established by that State
Contracting States may not accept oral declarations of baggage
Contracting States shall accept an oral declaration of baggage from passengers and crew
Contracting States shall accept an oral declaration of baggage only from passengers

qs.q: An aircraft flying to another Contracting State:
o: Is liable to pay customs duty on all unused fuel and oil carried
Is admitted temporarily free of customs duty only for the fuel and oil remaining
Is admitted to that State temporarily free of customs duty

qs.q: Before departure, a State shall not require the agent or PIC to deliver more than a set number of copies of the General Declaration, Cargo Manifest and stores list. These are:
o: 2 copies of the General Declaration and Cargo Manifest and one copy of a simple stores list
2 copies each of the General Declaration, Cargo Manifest and stores list
3 of each

qs.q: When a visitor travelling by air holds a valid passport and no visa is required, Contracting States:
o: Shall not require any other identity document from their consulates or operators before the flight
None of these
May in certain cases require another identity document

qs.q: The documents for entry and departure of aircraft:
o: Must be typewritten or produced electronically
Are accepted in handwritten block lettering in ink
Are accepted at the State's discretion
Aircraft registration, flight number, date and place of departure, destination, and number of crew and passengers
The nature of goods on board (e.g. dangerous goods)
A complete description of the payload (passengers, cargo and mail)

qs.q: What is the purpose of a Crew Member Certificate (CMC)?
o: To exempt flight crew from customs, health and immigration formalities on disembarking
To give aircrew access to the airside of an aerodrome
To identify aircrew

qs.q: What documents are required for persons travelling by air to enter a State?
o: Passport and confirmation of inclusion on the General Declaration passenger manifest
The same as if they arrived by ship
Passport, visa and any necessary health documents (vaccination certificates)
